findings.claim: 'A natural `new daMip_c()` would select the global `operator new`, which this image does not contain'
findings.measurement: FALSE. config/arm9/symbols.txt:1633 carries `_Znwj kind:function(arm,size=0xc) addr:0x0203cbe4`, and main carries src/_Znwj.cpp defining it. config/arm9/symbols.txt:1634 likewise carries `_ZdlPv` at 0x0203cbf0. The real, measured barrier is the one src/actors/Scuttlebug.cpp:196 states - 'Natural `new` selects the wrong allocator': the cartridge's factory calls fBase_c::operator new (_ZN7fBase_cnwEj), and mwccarm rejects an in-class operator new (include/fBase_c.h:150, accurately cited), so `new daMip_c()` would link but emit a call to the WRONG callee. The conclusion (keep the literal seam) is right; the stated reason is not, and the handoff's claim that Scuttlebug 'records the same measurement' misstates what Scuttlebug records. The committed source is clean on this point - include/daMip_c.h:153-156 and the src/actors/daMip_c.cpp classInit comment both state it correctly.
findings.note: include/fBase_c.h:155-157's own claim that the global _ZdlPv 'exists nowhere in this image' is contradicted by the same symbol table. Pre-existing on main, not this candidate's, but it is what the handoff leaned on.

findings.claim: Remaining debt is seven padding spans, mState, the daMip_cSelf shadow struct, one V3Blk block and the ov085 file statics.
findings.measurement: Materially understated on the dimension PIPELINE names ('Fields and object layout recovered versus raw-offset or shadow-struct accesses'). Measured in src/actors/daMip_c.cpp at this commit: 15 block-scope shadow-struct declarations across 9 distinct names (Mtx43 x4, Vector3 x3, V3 x2, Vector3_local, VObj, Obj, RG, G, V3Blk) - only daMip_cSelf and V3Blk are named; 63 block-scope extern declarations naming 26 distinct objects, several with contradictory types for the same object (data_ov085_021305c0 appears as int[], struct G, void*[] and char); and 18 `(char *)this` casts bound to c/self/p, driving 187 raw-offset accesses on 165 lines over 39 distinct offsets, 28 of them at or above 0x110. FOURTEEN of those 28 are offsets the header ALREADY names or types: all five typed sub-objects (0x110 mdCcAc_c, 0x144 mWithMeshClsn, 0x300 mModelAnim, 0x368 mShadowModel1, 0x3c0 mShadowModel2) plus 0x426 unk_426, 0x427 mTalkState, 0x429 mIsGlowing, 0x438 mPathId, 0x43c mRabbitId, 0x440 mCharacterId, 0x444 mNumPathNodes, 0x448 mPathNodeIndex and 0x45c mTalkingPlayer. The header's named fields are used ~97 times, so both spellings coexist throughout. Additionally mTalkingPlayer is documented in the header as 'A Player *' but declared s32 - the same debt class as mState, and unlisted.
findings.note: None of this is a byte defect and none of it is unusual for a first promotion. The defect is that the handoff's account of this dimension would lead a reader to the wrong conclusion, and PIPELINE requires the dimension recorded honestly.

source_review.summary: The design is right and the mechanics are right. The producer took the two-diagnostic structure, hoisted orphan_destination() so one fact decides what the reader is told, and split report_orphans() into a REWRITE class and a FIND OUT WHAT HAPPENED class. I tested that as a claim rather than reading the sentences: nothing in the destination-known section asserts a --reason refusal, a falling count, or a regression, and nothing in the destination-unknown section asserts 'Nothing regressed' or that --update absorbs it. VFY-2543-01, -02, -03 and -04 are retired as scoped. VFY-2543-08 is fixed -- the literal-set restatement tests are gone, orphan-plus-backslide is covered, and UpdateBehaviourPin actually runs --update. The printed `--update --reason` command works exactly as its paragraph says: exit 0, one attributed exceptions row, count down, follow-up --check green -- the documented escape hatch, not a new hole. Tests are 42 and 35, both exit 0 unpiped, and the suite is falsifiable: 11 of the 42 fail against attempt-1's tool while the three UpdateBehaviourPin tests pass against base, attempt 1 and attempt 2 -- the right result, and explained rather than assumed, because the `if args.update:` block is byte-identical at all three commits. TWO THINGS FAIL, both in the same family as the finding this commit was reworked for: a claim printed without being checked, and prose describing output the tool no longer produces. First, 'Nothing regressed. source_review.summary: Attempt 3 fixes what attempt 2 was failed for and finds a real defect neither the coordinator's brief nor my finding had scoped. destination_state() resolves three states and the diagnostic diverges at every split; the sentence 'Nothing regressed' is now printed only where a destination has been checked and passes, which I confirmed on the real tree rather than a synthetic one. The re-pointed epilogue guard is satisfiable and discriminates correctly on real data. The module docstring's new mode paragraph fixes VFY-2543-11 properly, why()'s docstring carries the same warning, and the rest of the docstring reads consistent end to end -- the --list flag it advertises exists, the count note is accurate, and the VFY-2543-06 laundering paragraph is correctly narrowed to the class --update actually absorbs and is not softened. The three declared mutants reproduce at 8 / 1 / 1 red with zero cross-talk. WHAT FAILS is the same defect one level finer, and it is live at 661 instances. destination_state() answers a question about the whole FILE; two lines above, rewrite_target() prints the ONE member identity the reader is told to create. For a multi-member destination those are different questions, and the failing-class block asserts the file's answer about the identity: 'not as a clean move', 'nothing regressed is not available here', 'the rewritten identity is a backslide the moment it exists'. Measured over every legacy_source row pointing at a failing destination: 2371 rows, of which 661 have a rewrite target that passes all five, spread across 122 of the 129 failing destinations. Proved end to end rather than inferred -- hand-rewriting src/_ZN7dBase_cD1Ev.cpp onto the target the tool itself printed makes --check exit 0, the clean move the block said was unavailable. The same claim is in the module docstring's failing bullet, and the replacement test test_nothing_regressed_is_claimed_only_where_the_destination_passes now requires the tool to withhold a true statement, so the suite pins the false claim rather than catching it: the gap moved one level rather than closing. Two smaller things. The failing-class block says 'Bank it with a reason, or fix the criterion named above' four lines before warning that --update --reason writes a permanent false row; the only command that banks with a reason IS --update --reason, and the two sentences differ only by an ordering the block never states -- measured, running it before the rewrite writes the false row, running it after writes nothing. And two verifier-built mutants leave all 56 tests green, both re-opening VFY-2543-10 through an untested arm of destination_state(): treating an absent scan as converted, and disabling the partially-scored guard -- with `scores=None` being that parameter's default, so the dangerous answer is the default answer. The gate mechanics are correct in all four classes and are not in question; every finding here is about guidance a reader acts on. No src/, header, config or ROM surface is touched; both config files are byte-identical to the base; no attribution surface is involved.

VFY-2543-06 is still open, still stated in both places, and not softened: a single --update on a clean-class orphan still exits 0, moves the baseline 2702 -> 2709 and writes no exception row. 0 live today, but the JUSTIFICATION is false about the code, so recording it. The producer's argument that the promise holds as written has two halves. The first is airtight: I enumerated all 36 combinations of (carried in {none,A,B}) x (manifest enrols {nothing,A}) x (0,1,2 enrolled members) x (destination tracked or not), and ZERO reach the `target is None` return with a clash defined -- a None target requires an identity carrying no symbol at all, which is mutually exclusive with a clash by construction. The second half is wrong. It says an untracked destination is absent from the ownership index 'because the index is built from the tracked tree'. It is not: srcpath._enrolment() builds the index by walking config/arm9/**/delinks.txt on DISK, keeping every entry that startswith('src/'), with no existence check and no git consultation, while tracked_sources() is `git ls-files src`. The two are independent by construction, and exactly one of the 36 combinations has a clash DEFINED BUT NOT NAMED: destination untracked, >1 enrolled member, carried symbol disagreeing -- the early 'it is not a tracked source file' return. I BUILT IT FROM REAL DATA: src/Cloud_Spawn.c#_ZN11daObjKumo_cD1Ev onto src/game/actors/d_a_obj_kumo.cpp (8 enrolled members, manifest enrols daObjKumo_c_classInit). With the destination tracked the state is 'converted' and the clash is named; with it untracked the state is 'unvouched', the detail is 'it is not a tracked source file', and the clash is silent. And the state is REACHABLE, not hypothetical: `git ls-files` omits a file that exists on disk but has not been `git add`ed (demonstrated in a throwaway repo), so during the very workflow that creates orphans -- delinks row edited, destination written, not yet staged -- the destination is enrolled-with-many-members AND untracked. WHY THIS IS A NOTE AND NOT A FAIL, by the same bar I have used for four rounds (a reader-facing claim false on live data at scale): it is 0-live twice over (0 of 9008 ownership keys untracked, 0 of 136 promoted destinations untracked, 0 of 651 carried symbols disagreeing -- two independently-zero conditions must coincide), and in that state the report tells the reader NOT to rewrite ('no rewrite target this tool can vouch for'), so the missing clash costs no actionable advice. THE SHARP EDGE is that the test pins the false premise with assertEqual(TR.rewrite_target(carried, 'src/Vanished.cpp', {}, SYMBOLS), 'src/Vanished.cpp') -- it passes {} as the ownership index, which assumes the premise rather than proving it. THE ONE-LINE FIX is to qualify the docstring ('in every state that names a target') and re-aim that assertion at rewrite_target(carried, dest, {dest: ['A','B']}, SYMBOLS) == dest + '#' + carried, which is the shape that actually occurs; because of VFY-2543-22's docstring assertion the test must be edited in the same commit.

The tree has no live instance (0 of 651 carried-symbol identities disagree, reproduced), so I built one: on src/Cloud_Spawn.c the clash is named in the converted, failing and unvouched arms, is silent on agreement and silent for a bare identity, and reaches the printed report (ctl-P6). Attempt 4's control G, the probe that produced this finding, now carries the text. Four mutants pin it, including one that swaps the two sides of the comparison.

CLOSED FOR EVERYTHING THE TOOL PRINTS, which is what the finding was about. promotion_census() derives the population from arguments report_orphans() already holds and agrees field for field with a census I compute separately and with the ten figures I re-derived from the raw manifest: 2359 / 136 / 7 / 129 / 0 / 2329 / 620 / 1709 / 0 / 122. The memo is keyed on the destination and saves 2223 destination_state() calls. Crucially the three mutant shapes that left 69 of 69 green on attempt 4 now redden two tests each, and the printed-population test also asserts the five old literals are ABSENT so they cannot be typed back in beside the computed ones. The module docstring's figures stay frozen, and I verified rather than accepted the reason: nothing runs a scan at module level, import costs 100.8 ms against 3439.8 ms for a scan, and with git off PATH the import succeeds while tracked_sources() raises FileNotFoundError -- so computing a census into a docstring would both multiply every import (tu_promote's included) by ~34x and turn a working import into a hard failure wherever git is unavailable. Dating the prose and stating that the report wins where they disagree is honest, not a dodge; the one cheaper remedy I would have proposed -- a test comparing the prose figures to live data -- is worse, because it would go red on every unrelated promotion that legitimately moves 2,359.

CLOSED AS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN AS WORDING. 'leaving `count` unchanged' is retired; the block now computes after = len((banked - identities) | targets), counts how many targets are banked already, and prints which arm applies with both outcomes explained. The underlying claim is true verbatim: tools/tu_promote.py:249 is literally `if target not in converted`, after line 246 removes both spellings of the legacy key and with count recomputed from the list, and 645 of the 2359 pairs name an already-banked target. The formula agrees with a simulation of those same lines in both cases (2702 -> 2701 already banked, 2702 -> 2702 not), and three controls confirm it as printed: ctl-P1 '1 of the 1 ... 2702 -> 2701', ctl-P2 '0 of the 1 ... 2702 -> 2702', ctl-P3 '1 of the 2 ... 2703 -> 2702'. That is the right direction for a promise this tree has no live instance of. findings.detail: TWO THINGS THE SUITE STILL CANNOT NOTICE, NEITHER A DEFECT, both found by my own mutants and both left surviving on purpose rather than hidden. (1) The ORDER of the two early `unvouched` returns is unpinned: swapping them leaves 75 of 75 green. I characterised the delta rather than assuming it -- over the 36 combinations the STATE differs in 0, the TARGET in 0, and the detail in exactly 1: an untracked destination whose target is also None would say 'it is scored per member and no manifest row here enrolls ... under a symbol' instead of 'it is not a tracked source file'. The swap never drops a clash (that combination carries no symbol, so none is defined). The shipped order is the better one -- the untracked fact is the more urgent of the two -- and the state is 0-live twice over: 0 of the 2,050 bare banked identities are moved with no manifest row onto a multi-member destination, and 0 promoted destinations are untracked. Not worth a test on today's evidence; recorded so the next round does not rediscover it. (2) The docstring's CORRECTION paragraph -- the one that says the old argument was false and why -- is not pinned: deleting it leaves 75 of 75 green. The PROMISE is pinned, and the BEHAVIOUR is pinned twice (drop the clash from the untracked arm, or revert the hoist, and the test reddens), so a future edit cannot make the tool wrong silently -- only the explanation of why it is right could be lost. Pinning explanatory prose to a test is the pattern I argued against in the polish round, so I am recording this rather than asking for it.

source_review.summary: The production fix I asked for, taken rather than deflected, and it holds up under attack. The hoist changes no state and no target over a 1,920-input product, so no row can change group; the only detail changes are the untracked arm gaining the clash; the newly-unguarded rewrite_target() call raised on none of 363 malformed inputs and costs nothing measurable; every other function in the file is byte-identical to the parent, and --check and the bare run are byte-identical on the real tree. source_review.summary: First source review of ov043/daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c at this commit, derived independently of the byte-only pass of 2026-09-07; that pass was treated as hearsay and none of its numbers were carried forward. Producer session was prod-kuruma-0907; this reviewer is fleet-0907-vfy-kuruma-adopt-0909, a different session, and attribution.json preserves the original per-member authors across the fold (tangosdev for D1, D0, InitResources and classInit; lunavyqo for CleanupResources) rather than reassigning them to the promoter. FAKE SLOT INTERFACE: absent, and proved rather than assumed. src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km1_kurumajiku.cpp and include/daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c.h contain no cast over `this`, no fabricated slot struct, no manual vtable indexing and no mNN offset member; a grep for that whole pattern family over the TU and both headers returns nothing. The positive proof is romdata_check: the class's emitted _ZTV21daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c compares equal to the cartridge for the full 128 bytes, all 32 slots, with relocations resolved -- so every slot target is the ROM's target, not merely a load+blx of the right shape. Reading the two images by hand confirms the leaf vtable is word-identical to daObjKurumajiku_c's ov002 table at 0x02109320 except at slots 0, 3, 16 and 17, which are exactly the four the header declares; nothing is silently inherited and nothing extra is overridden. The base's slots 0 and 3 are 0x00000000 in the cartridge, which is the `= 0` the base header spells, and no .text byte gate can see that. NAME PROVENANCE: the class name is ROM-evidenced, not coined. _ZTS at ov043 0x02112350 holds the NUL-terminated '21daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c' and the _ZTI record at 0x02112338 points its middle word at that address; the retired tree spelling RickshawBdw appears nowhere in the image. The _ZTI third word is 0x021092f8 = _ZTI17daObjKurumajiku_c, an __si_class_type_info with one base at subobject offset 0, so the intermediate base the header asserts is stated by the cartridge; the D1 literal pool at 0x02111440 corroborates it independently with three vptr words (0x0211238c, 0x02109320, 0x0210ae38). The base class name daObjKurumajiku_c is likewise ROM-evidenced from ov002 _ZTS at 0x02109304. Method spellings InitResources, CleanupResources, Behavior, Render and the classInit suffix are the tree's established reconstructions carried in symbols.txt, not names this change invents; the ROM preserves no mangled member names. Coined and disclosed, not disguised: the local struct names ResourceDescriptor and Km1KurumajikuProfile (the latter field-for-field identical to the adjacent sibling d_a_obj_km1_kuruma.cpp's Km1KurumaProfile, one of 6 sources using those field names) and, in the unchanged base header, the placeholder field name mMountedActorIds, which is labelled a placeholder in situ while its 0x320 offset and 4x4 width are the observed facts. ADDRESS-DERIVED PLACEHOLDERS: exactly three in the reviewed TU -- func_ov002_020b6c54, func_ov002_020b6ac8 and data_ov043_02112344 -- plus two prose mentions of func_ov002_ names in the base header. All three are the live spellings in config/arm9/overlays/ov002/symbols.txt and ov043/symbols.txt, all three are disclosed in comments naming the literal pool they were read from, and check_references confirms no reference in the change resolves to nothing. There are no unk_ members and no cast standing in for a type other than the deliberately opaque three-word ResourceDescriptor, whose extent is bounded by _ZTS starting at 0x02112350 and whose third word points at a 'CLPS' collision blob at 0x02111bc0 -- consistent with the comment, which correctly declines to guess its members. RELOCATED WORDS: every address the source names was resolved to a configured symbol by hand rather than trusted from a byte match -- 0x020b6c54 and 0x020b6ac8 to the ov002 helper placeholders, 0x02109320 and 0x0210ae38 to _ZTV17daObjKurumajiku_c and _ZTV10dBgActor_c, 0x020b6b38 and 0x020b6b10 to daObjKurumajiku_c's own Behavior and Render, and the two classInit BL words decoded to 0x02043444 = _ZN7fBase_cnwEj and 0x020eea50 = _ZN10dBgActor_cC2Ev, which is what the header's `operator new` and implicit-constructor account requires. The InitResources constant 0x88 is checked against the KM1_KURUMA profile at 0x02112438, whose id half really is 0x0088, one below this class's 0x0089. .DATA POINTER WORDS: the rename hazard is closed in-commit. The four member symbols and the vtable are renamed from the RickshawBdw spelling inside config/arm9/overlays/ov043/symbols.txt in the same commit as the source, symbols/actor_renames.tsv gains the five matching rows, check_rename_ledger agrees every mangled and vtable row with its module's symbols.txt, and romdata_check reports zero differing words for this source -- so no pointer word links as 0. delinks.txt collapses the five legacy entries into one entry over 0x021113fc..0x02111518 with no gap and no overlap against the ukishima and kuruma neighbours, and the manifest's tiling arithmetic (0x50+0x64+0x14+0x18+0x3c = 0x11c) is correct. Each underlying claim was re-derived from the ROM in this session and holds, and each citation still resolves on a fresh clone through the symbols/actor_renames.tsv row this same commit adds, so the evidence chain is intact. source_review.summary: Independent integration-stage source review, authored in session fleet-0907-int-adopt-0909 and derived from the files themselves rather than inherited from the 2026-09-09 verifier. I read the whole reconstructed TU, both headers, the manifest, the ov043 symbols.txt and delinks.txt deltas, the appended actor_renames.tsv rows and both queue rows. WHAT THE SOURCE CLAIMS AND WHY IT HOLDS. src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km1_kurumajiku.cpp declares five members and defines three of them, leaving the D1/D0 pair to the inline empty destructor in include/daObjKm1_Kurumajiku_c.h, which is the documented way to get mwccarm 2004/b56 to emit D1 before D0 and no leaf D2; the file states this in its own comment rather than leaving it to be rediscovered. The functions are written in the reverse of ROM address order, which is what mwccarm's reverse-source-order .text emission requires, and the comment says so and says the build refuses the object otherwise. The claimed run 0x021113fc..0x02111518 is derived by address and tiles exactly: 0x50 + 0x64 + 0x14 + 0x18 + 0x3c = 0x11c, bounded below by d_a_obj_km1_ukishima.cpp and above by d_a_obj_km1_kuruma.cpp, and the delinks.txt delta shows the five legacy one-function entries collapsing into that single range, which is the arithmetic I checked rather than took on trust. The header declares exactly the four slots the ROM's leaf vtable differs at (0, 3, 16, 17) and explicitly refuses to redeclare slots 6 and 9 because those words are daObjKurumajiku_c's own ov002 Behavior and Render, so no override is silently inherited and none is fabricated. There is no fake slot interface, no unk_ member, no offset cast and no magic address dispatch anywhere in the TU. issue.body:
# Finish Spiny shadow reconstruction and complete-object ownership

PR #2863 edits the existing, unenrolled Spiny shadow TU. Local repair `3568a524fe60c5dfa2f3d4ff83451a1b3d11515a` replaces the fabricated Render interface and contradictory state-helper declaration with real calls. The producer reports all 34 functions still match and the complete object remains identical. That repair is local; this issue does not assert publication, independent acceptance or promotion.

Next owner: `codex-integrator-0920`, coordinating separately reserved producer and reviewer work.

- Replace the byte-plus-padding matrix field and aggregate overlays with evidenced real fields, checking every shared-header consumer. Reconstruct the remaining raw helper/state views and ordinary member interfaces without changing relocated bytes.
- Establish the production class identity from the ROM's `daTgz_c` RTTI. Preserve the explicit distinction between that identity and the current community-named Spiny shadow.
- Resolve complete-object ownership and destructor order before promotion. Fresh producer measurements retain nine unlicensed emitted outputs and the reversed D1/D0 ordinal pair; a text match alone does not resolve them.
- Preserve every function's attribution and enrollment identity. Keep the TU in `src_tu/` until the source, complete-object, metadata, relocation and full-ROM gates support a production move.

Remaining matrix and source reconstruction is partial (SP2863-03/04). Correctness findings must be repaired rather than deferred, and any claimed compiler limitation requires a reproducible pinned experiment. Require independent acceptance of the exact candidate and current base before merging.

issue.body:
# Finish BookShot shadow interfaces and complete-object ownership

PR #2868 replaces raw member offsets in the existing BookShot/BookShotSpawner/Bookend shadow TU. Independent checks at `47ee06b41539d307052a7af1b1c1e602bb386f6a` reproduce all 31 functions / 6,040 bytes, with no differing or blind words; the complete object is identical to parent `9022c77b3834c5ee77c31b4fb4af587418137d6c`. This establishes the narrow cleanup's byte neutrality, not finished source reconstruction or promotion.

Next owner: `codex-integrator-0920`, coordinating separately reserved producer and reviewer work.

- Replace the 48-byte matrix overlay beginning at `unk_1ec` and the vector overlay over `unk_438/unk_43c/unk_440` with evidenced real fields. Verify every affected header consumer.
- Reconstruct the remaining raw field helpers, mangled-name bridges and address-access macro using actual class interfaces. Measure ordinary Clear, Update, SetPosRelativeToActor and UpdateYoshiEat calls; do not assert that cleaner forms fail without a pinned experiment.
- Resolve complete-object ownership and lifecycle order before promotion. Independent parent/head checks retain 17 unlicensed emitted outputs, missing compiler-only policies for BookShot D2, BookShotSpawner D2 and Vector3 D1, and the two destructor-order exceptions. Both complete TU checks currently exit with failure despite all text functions matching.
- Preserve symbol credits, actual class-identity evidence and enrollment. Keep this an explicit shadow until complete-object, metadata, relocation and full-ROM checks justify production enrollment.

Track BOOK2868-02/03 as remaining reconstruction/ownership work. This issue does not certify unreviewed surrounding contracts, claim that the PR has merged, or turn the validator's `noverify` result into compiler proof. Require independent source acceptance for the exact candidate and current base.

# Finish BookShot shadow interfaces and complete-object ownership

PR #2868 replaces raw member offsets in the existing BookShot/BookShotSpawner/Bookend shadow TU. Independent checks at `47ee06b41539d307052a7af1b1c1e602bb386f6a` reproduce all 31 functions / 6,040 bytes, with no differing or blind words; the complete object is identical to parent `9022c77b3834c5ee77c31b4fb4af587418137d6c`. This establishes the narrow cleanup's byte neutrality, not finished source reconstruction or promotion.

Next owner: `codex-integrator-0920`, coordinating separately reserved producer and reviewer work.

- Replace the 48-byte matrix overlay beginning at `unk_1ec` and the vector overlay over `unk_438/unk_43c/unk_440` with evidenced real fields. Verify every affected header consumer.
- Reconstruct the remaining raw field helpers, mangled-name bridges and address-access macro using actual class interfaces. Measure ordinary Clear, Update, SetPosRelativeToActor and UpdateYoshiEat calls; do not assert that cleaner forms fail without a pinned experiment.
- Resolve complete-object ownership and lifecycle order before promotion. Independent parent/head checks retain 17 unlicensed emitted outputs, missing compiler-only policies for BookShot D2, BookShotSpawner D2 and Vector3 D1, and the two destructor-order exceptions. Both complete TU checks currently exit with failure despite all text functions matching.
- Preserve symbol credits, actual class-identity evidence and enrollment. Keep this an explicit shadow until complete-object, metadata, relocation and full-ROM checks justify production enrollment.

Track BOOK2868-02/03 as remaining reconstruction/ownership work. This issue does not certify unreviewed surrounding contracts, claim that the PR has merged, or turn the validator's `noverify` result into compiler proof. Require independent source acceptance for the exact candidate and current base.

issue.body:
# Finish BookShot shadow interfaces and complete-object ownership

PR #2868 replaces raw member offsets in the existing BookShot/BookShotSpawner/Bookend shadow TU. Independent checks at `47ee06b41539d307052a7af1b1c1e602bb386f6a` reproduce all 31 functions / 6,040 bytes, with no differing or blind words; the complete object is identical to parent `9022c77b3834c5ee77c31b4fb4af587418137d6c`. This establishes the narrow cleanup's byte neutrality, not finished source reconstruction or promotion.

Next owner: `codex-integrator-0920`, coordinating separately reserved producer and reviewer work.

- Replace the 48-byte matrix overlay beginning at `unk_1ec` and the vector overlay over `unk_438/unk_43c/unk_440` with evidenced real fields. Verify every affected header consumer.
- Reconstruct the remaining raw field helpers, mangled-name bridges and address-access macro using actual class interfaces. Measure ordinary Clear, Update, SetPosRelativeToActor and UpdateYoshiEat calls; do not assert that cleaner forms fail without a pinned experiment.
- Resolve complete-object ownership and lifecycle order before promotion. Independent parent/head checks retain 17 unlicensed emitted outputs, missing compiler-only policies for BookShot D2, BookShotSpawner D2 and Vector3 D1, and the two destructor-order exceptions. Both complete TU checks currently exit with failure despite all text functions matching.
- Preserve symbol credits, actual class-identity evidence and enrollment. Keep this an explicit shadow until complete-object, metadata, relocation and full-ROM checks justify production enrollment.

Track BOOK2868-02/03 as remaining reconstruction/ownership work. This issue does not certify unreviewed surrounding contracts, claim that the PR has merged, or turn the validator's `noverify` result into compiler proof. Require independent source acceptance for the exact candidate and current base.

R1.reason: Verified. There are nine non-virtual members. The symbols.txt rows are renamed in place at the same addresses and sizes, and the manifest symbol fields and attribution keys follow them. The .data PMF records 0x02130ba4..0x02130be4 (relocs.txt, by address) and __sinit_ov084_02130654 still map table slots 0 to 8 to 0x0212fc10, fa7c, f6d8, f630, f588, f460, f33c, f2dc and f298, which are Wait, Sleep, Bite, Wake, Doze, Die, Shrink, Gone and Regrow. Each coined name agrees with its body. Wait sets full scale and moves to state 1 when mPlayerDist < 0x4b0000. Sleep plays the snore loop sound and moves to 3 on a close, fast player, with bubble-pop particles. Bite plays the lunge, uses the head cylinder and hurts the player. Wake runs its timer, then sets the lunge anim and moves to 2. Doze returns to 1 or bites again. Die plays particles and moves to 6. Shrink scales down, spawns 0x122 and moves to 7. Gone stays hidden until dist > 0x4b0000. Regrow scales up and returns to 0. The names are marked coined in the header. No consumer in src or include names the old symbols.

The fix is to regenerate the note on a CLEAN BASE CHECKOUT and diff that against the head, which is how the per-measure split in section 2 was derived. A PR that silently carries someone else's numbers is how a generated file's staleness becomes invisible.
2b_method_traps_worth_reusing.validate_merge_parent_order: validate_merge --require-merge-commit requires the BASE as the merge's FIRST parent, which is the CI shape. A restack merges main INTO the branch, so the branch is first and the tool refuses with 'committed merge first parent 58a735d6ff is not base 115cb5d748'. Do not drop --require-merge-commit to get past it: build a THROWAWAY merge in CI parent order (git merge --no-ff <head> from base), confirm its tree sha equals the head's tree sha, run validate_merge there, then delete the probe branch. Probe accff0c01 had parents 115cb5d74 and fb3babaef and a tree identical to fb3babaef; it was never pushed and has been deleted.

source_review.summary: First genuine source review of ov045/daObjKm2_Ukishima_c; the 2026-09-07 pass is treated as byte evidence only and nothing in it was carried over. Base: I measured git merge-base origin/main 5a642c837 as b0d348e536fb3304b6ab12d88fe95d780cbeb91d and confirmed the task's declared fd55979f074c7ad796e2846328933363315e7f06 is a strict ancestor of it, so the declared value is stale and the measured fork point is used as both tested_base and reviewed_base. The producer's own handoff note records the same b0d348e53 as the base as shipped, which corroborates the measurement independently. VERDICT RESTS ON THIS: the class model is proved twice over by two methods that could each have refuted it. By hand, the emitted vtable differs from its parent daObjUkiyuka_c at exactly four slots, 0, 3, 16 and 17, and the header declares exactly four things, an inline destructor plus CleanupResources and InitResources; the differing set and the declared set coincide with nothing left over on either side, and slots 6 and 9 are the parent's own Behavior and Render, correctly not redeclared. By tool, romdata_check verifies _ZTV19daObjKm2_Ukishima_c at 128 bytes, all 32 slots relocation-resolved against the cartridge, so this is slot identity and not merely slot shape. The 32-slot length is itself consistent with the dBgActor_c line rather than the 31-slot dActor_c line. NAMES: daObjKm2_Ukishima_c is ROM-attested, not coined; ov045 0x02112f14 holds the NUL-terminated '19daObjKm2_Ukishima_c' and the _ZTI record at 0x02112efc points its middle word at exactly that address, while _ZTI+8 at 0x02112f04 holds 0x02109104, which ov002 names _ZTI14daObjUkiyuka_c and which fixes the base. Retiring the coined FloatingFloorBfs is therefore the ruling applied correctly. The five symbols.txt rows were renamed IN PLACE in this same commit with no alias row and no bounding row added, which is what keeps the .data pointer words resolving by name; had the rename landed without the same-commit symbols.txt edit, those words would link as 0 and no byte gate would have seen it, so this was checked directly and the vtable and profile both verify byte-equal. Because tools/match.py wildcards relocated words, no call target was accepted on byte equality: every branch and literal-pool word in the 0x02111b14..0x02111c30 run was resolved by symbol name instead, and all of them, fBase_c::operator new, dBgActor_cC2Ev, the dBgW_KcMbg and Model member destructors, dActor_cD2Ev, Memory::Deallocate and GAME_HEAP_PTR, are what the source says they are. NO FABRICATED SLOT INTERFACE: the hierarchy is real C++ inheritance through daObjUkiyuka_c to dBgActor_c, there is no struct of function pointers cast over this, no offset-cast dispatch, and no m<hex> member anywhere in the reviewed class, which has no fields of its own at all. The base declares both overridden methods as virtual s32 ...() = 0 with return types matching the derived declarations, so these are genuine overrides and not the silent-inherit trap that an undeclared override would produce. The parent's pure slots are literal zero words in the cartridge, which the differential confirms. DISCLOSED DEBT, none of it disguised: three address-derived placeholders remain, func_ov002_020b6584, func_ov002_020b6424 and data_ov045_02112f08, all three of which are the tree's own existing symbol names rather than anything invented here, each disclosed in the source with the reason and with the descriptor declared and not defined so the entry claims .text only; the local UkishimaSpawnInfo type and its field names are coined and labelled as coined, and their layout is nevertheless proved because romdata_check verifies the whole 28-byte g_profile_KM2_UKISHIMA record against the cartridge. The route is text-only, which the manifest states is a scope decision and not a codegen limitation, and the sibling that already landed in this overlay took the same route. The delinks run collapse was checked rather than assumed: all 29 ov045 .text entries sort into a sequence with zero gaps and zero overlaps, and the five absorbed sizes tile the claimed run exactly. SCOPE CORRECTION, reported and not silently absorbed: the task named include/FloatingFloorLllSmall.h, which this commit does not touch at all; it belongs to ov022 and to a different class. The header this commit actually retires is include/FloatingFloorBfs.h. I read both, and both are listed below. Separately, and out of scope here, FloatingFloorLllSmall is itself a coined name the cartridge contradicts, since ov022 0x021140c0 reads '17daObjFl_Ukiyuka_c'; that is a pre-existing defect of the same shape this commit fixes and it is left untouched, correctly. UNVERIFIED AND STATED AS SUCH: the cross-class claim that the other leaf daObjFl_Ukiyuka_c allocates 0x330 was not re-measured here, because this class's own 0x32c is proved directly by the immediate at 0x02111bf8 and by the size assert, and the larger sibling only supports the base's boundary argument, which belongs to daObjUkiyuka_c rather than to this entry. No correctness finding and no provenance finding is left open; the three findings recorded below are all disposed.

source_review.summary: Independent integration-stage source review, authored in session fleet-0907-int-adopt-0909 and derived from the files themselves rather than inherited from the 2026-09-09 verifier. I read the whole reconstructed TU, the new header, the header this commit retires as it stands at the base, the two neighbouring headers it edits, the manifest, the ov045 symbols.txt and delinks.txt deltas, the five appended actor_renames.tsv rows and the queue rows. WHAT THE SOURCE CLAIMS AND WHY IT HOLDS. src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km2_ukishima.cpp declares five members and defines three, leaving the D1/D0 pair to the inline empty destructor in include/daObjKm2_Ukishima_c.h, which is the documented way to make mwccarm 2004/b56 emit D1 before D0 and no leaf D2; the retired header declared that destructor OUT OF LINE, so this is a deliberate lever and not an accident of transcription. Functions are written in the reverse of ROM address order, as mwccarm's reverse-source-order .text emission requires. The claimed run 0x02111b14..0x02111c30 tiles exactly: 0x50 + 0x64 + 0x14 + 0x18 + 0x3c = 0x11c, bounded below by src/d_a_obj_km2_nobiru.c and above by src/game/actors/d_a_obj_km2_gura.cpp, and the delinks.txt delta shows the five legacy one-function entries collapsing into that single range, which is arithmetic I re-did rather than took on trust. The header records the RTTI group at ov045 0x02112efc, 0x02112f14 and 0x02112f50, states that 0x02112f50 is the address point because 0x02112f48 is the offset-to-top zero and 0x02112f4c is the typeinfo address, and derives the base daObjUkiyuka_c both from typeinfo plus eight and from the three vptr stores in the destructor pools. It declares exactly the four slots the leaf table differs at, 0, 3, 16 and 17, and explicitly refuses to redeclare slots 6 and 9 because those words are daObjUkiyuka_c's own ov002 Behavior and Render. There is no fake slot interface, no unk_ member, no offset cast and no magic address dispatch anywhere in the TU. The size assertion 0x32c is a compile-time typedef rather than a comment. CleanupResources is identified as the key function that anchors the vtable group, which matches the header's inline destructor and is the reason the TU emits the RTTI group at all. INTEGRATION JUDGMENT. The change carries its own queue-row refresh: notes/data/tu-promotion-queue.tsv replaces the FloatingFloorBfs row with a daObjKm2_Ukishima_c row and flips already_promoted from no to yes, so merging this does not by itself make the queue row stale. The rename is closed in the same commit across symbols.txt, delinks.txt, the manifest and actor_renames.tsv, and check_rename_ledger is green on the merged tree. The two neighbouring headers it edits, include/daObjUkiyuka_c.h and include/daDsnBase_c.h, are prose-only edits that retire the coined spelling in the exact places that cited it, which is the right blast radius rather than a tree-wide sweep smuggled into a class change.
